Generate a flat, seamless, tileable tangent-space normal map texture for a heavily embossed silver metal material featuring baroque floral relief carving with roses, acanthus scrolls, and filigree ornamentation.

Two reference images are provided:
- Image 1: A photorealistic PBR preview sphere showing the embossed silver material under studio lighting, used as the sole source of surface relief depth, emboss height, carving structure, and micro-detail logic.
- Image 2: The flat Base Color / Albedo map for the same material, used as the exact layout anchor. The normal map output must be perfectly pixel-aligned to this albedo map.

Surface relief extraction rules (from the sphere only):
- Raised elements: rose bloom petals and centers sit at high elevation with smooth rounded forms, acanthus leaf scrolls curl upward with strong emboss height, stem and vine elements are rounded ridges above the base plate, filigree curls have tight raised edges with soft inner slopes
- Recessed elements: engraved line details between scrolls sit below the surrounding relief, the flat base metal plate is the lowest depth level, carved shadow channels along petal edges and leaf veins define edge depth transitions
- Micro-detail: faint brushed metal directionality on flat base areas, fine engraved crosshatch or line texturing inside recessed channel zones, subtle surface grain across all areas
- Depth hierarchy from lowest to highest: base plate < engraved channels < flat relief ground < scroll bodies < leaf forms < rose petal layers < rose center peak

Normal map generation rules:
- Use the albedo map as the strict layout anchor. Every carved element, rose, scroll, leaf, and filigree curl in the albedo must have a correctly oriented normal deflection in the output.
- Do not preserve the circular sphere boundary. Flatten and unwrap the surface logic into a seamless rectangular tile.
- Remove all sphere curvature normals. Remove all 3D globe shading or radial depth bowing caused by the sphere form.
- Remove all lighting, shadows, specular highlights, reflections, ambient occlusion, and any baked illumination.
- Do not invent depth or shapes not supported by the albedo layout or sphere surface observation.
- Do not convert color variation alone into false depth unless it clearly corresponds to confirmed physical relief.
- Ensure the output tiles seamlessly on all four edges with no visible seams, no edge-specific lighting discontinuities, and no border artifacts. The pattern must repeat cleanly horizontally and vertically.

Output specification:
- Format: one single flat texture image, full tile, no sphere shape, no background, no labels, no borders, no multiple views
- Color space: standard OpenGL tangent-space normal map encoding
  - Flat surface normals pointing straight up encode as RGB (128, 128, 255) mid blue-purple
  - Left-facing surface normals shift red channel low
  - Right-facing surface normals shift red channel high
  - Down-facing normals shift green channel low
  - Up-facing normals shift green channel high
  - Deep emboss peaks have high blue-green intensity, steep carved walls show strong red-green deflection
- The dominant base tone of the output should be the flat-normal mid blue-purple (128, 128, 255) where the base plate is flat
- Strong red-green channel deflection along all emboss edges, scroll curves, petal slopes, and leaf forms
- High blue channel saturation at the tops of raised rose centers and scroll peaks
- Sharp normal transitions at engraved channel edges, smooth gradient slopes across petal and leaf body surfaces
- Seamless and tileable on all edges
- Production-ready, game-engine compatible, PBR workflow standard
- No lighting information baked into the output
- No ambient occlusion encoded in the output

This is an image-to-image generation task. You are provided with:
- A photorealistic PBR sphere preview of the material (reference for surface relief and occlusion logic)
- A flat Base Color / Albedo map of the same material (use as layout anchor for pattern placement and tiling structure)

Your output must be a single flat grayscale AO texture reconstructed from the surface logic observed across both inputs.

- Deep occlusion in the tight spiral centers of each sculpted rose, where overlapping petals create enclosed cavities
- Strong occlusion in the undersides of curling acanthus leaf tips and volute scroll terminations where the relief curls back under itself
- Medium-dark occlusion along the narrow channels and grooves between adjacent raised stems, scrolls, and leaf forms where geometry crowds together
- Moderate occlusion at the base of all raised relief elements where embossed forms meet the recessed flat metal background plate
- Subtle occlusion along the inner edges of each petal layer transition and leaf rib where surfaces fold slightly inward
- The flat recessed background metal plate between all relief elements should be light grey, slightly darkened only immediately adjacent to raised forms
- The highest exposed peaks of rose petals, outer scroll edges, and upward-facing leaf surfaces should be near white — fully unoccluded
- Maintain smooth gradient falloff from occluded crevices to exposed peaks — no hard edges, no banding

WHAT TO STRICTLY EXCLUDE:
- No directional lighting or shading baked in from the sphere render
- No specular highlights or metallic reflections
- No broad spherical shading gradient from the preview render
- No cast shadows from one element onto another surface
- No circular sphere boundary or cropped composition
- No dark areas caused by the sphere's edge falloff
- No color — pure grayscale only
- No labels, borders, frames, or watermarks
- No invented deep occlusion on areas that are geometrically flat

- Format: Single flat square texture image
- Mode: Grayscale only (no color channels)
- Value mapping: White (255) = fully exposed, unoccluded surface peak / Black (0) = deepest enclosed cavity or tight crevice / Mid grey = recessed background plate between relief

- Tileability: Fully seamless and tileable on all four edges — no visible seams, no edge-specific darkening, no lighting discontinuities at borders
- Relief intensity: High — this material has strong, deep sculptural relief with significant height variation, so the AO map should show clear contrast between recessed crevices and exposed peaks, while the flat background plate remains a consistent mid-to-light grey
- Production standard: Clean, game-ready, PBR pipeline compatible ambient occlusion map with no lighting baked in

Generate a flat, seamless, tileable grayscale PBR Roughness map for a heavily engraved oxidized silver metal material featuring baroque floral relief work with roses, acanthus scrolls, and ornate botanical motifs.

- Output must be a pure black and white grayscale image only, no color tint whatsoever
- Darker pixels mean smoother and more reflective surface
- Lighter pixels mean rougher and more matte surface
- Do not bake in any lighting, shading, shadows, ambient occlusion, specular highlights, or reflected environment
- Do not preserve the circular boundary of the sphere in any way
- Do not include any background, border, label, or compositional element from the sphere render
- Flatten all surface roughness information into a straight-on seamless tile perfectly matching the albedo map layout
- The texture must tile seamlessly and repeat cleanly on all four edges with no visible seams, no edge lighting discontinuities, and no artifacts
- Do not invent roughness variation not supported by the material observed on the sphere
- Do not confuse bright lit areas on the sphere with smooth surface, read only the material finish logic

- Single image output only, no multiple views, no annotations, no guides
